newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO AND VALENCIA OUT OF SPANISH CUP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DEPORTIVO AND VALENCIA OUT OF SPANISH CUP.

text.p: Valencia crashed out of the Spanish Cup on Wednesday to second division Las Palmas after squandering a 2-0 league from the first leg before finally losing on penalties.

1995 winners Deportivo Coruna are also out after the goalless draw at Espanyol, who go through on the away-goals rule. They join Real Betis, Racing Santander, Celta Vigo and holders Atletico Madrid in Friday's quarter-final draw.
Of the sides in action on Wednesday, Valencia had seemed the most likely side to go through to the last eight after taking the away leg.
But Las Palmas played a fine game, and there were shouts of protest against the club board after the penalty miss by Argentine defender Fernando Caceres which cost Valencia the tie.
Deportivo were unable to take their tie despite playing most of their fourth-round match against an Espanyol side reduced to 10 men.
Deportivo started strongly and hit the bar twice in the opening minutes but were unable to break down fierce Espanyol resistance in the second half. The first leg had ended 2-2.
"We played with all the ingredients we had, but they weren't enough," said Deportivo manager John Toshack "We've lacked bite up-front for many weeks."

Atletic Bilbao, winners of the Cup 23 times, went behind to an early goal against Racing Santander who hung on for a 1-1 draw despite being reduced to just nine men. Racing's 1-0 victory in the first leg was enough to take them through.
Celta Vigo were unexpectedly pressurised in the 0-0 draw with second division Lleida, but went through on the away-goals rule thanks to the late equaliser scored in the first-leg 1-1 draw.
The most impressive performance came from in-form Real Betis. Betis beat UEFA Cup side Tenerife 3-0 to win the tie 5-0 on aggregate.
Cup holders Atletico Madrid beat Compostela 3-2 on Tuesday night, to take their quarter-final berth with a comfortable 5-2 aggregate win.
Real Madrid will have to turn around a 3-2 first-leg defeat in Thursday's big clash against arch-rivals Barcelona, while Rayo Vallecano travel to Extremadura after a 2-2 draw last week.
